target.title: test(gateway): lock config mutation allowlist contract
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `gateway` built-in tool is a **persistent control-plane write surface**: agent-driven `config.apply` / `config.patch` can change live gateway config without operator CLI involvement. Per `SECURITY.md` and [Control plane tools risk](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security#control-plane-tools-risk), **the model/agent is not a trusted principal** — the runtime must fail closed and only permit a narrow, hand-maintained allowlist.

That allowlist lives in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts:54` as `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS`. Today it is a **mutable string array with no contract lock**:

| Existing coverage | What it proves | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway-tool-guard-coverage.test.ts` (~43 behavioral cases) | Many real patches are allowed/blocked (auth, plugins, sandbox, hooks, MCP, etc.) | Does **not** fail when someone adds/removes/reorders allowlist patterns |
| `gateway-tool.test.ts` | Tool schema exposes `replacePaths`; description mentions it | Does **not** exercise guard semantics with `replacePaths` |
| `src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts` | Gateway RPC rejects destructive array shrinks without `replacePaths` | Tests **server merge policy**, not the gateway-tool path allowlist after merge |

**Risk without this PR:** a maintainer can widen the agent-tunable surface (e.g. add `plugins.allow`, `gateway.auth.token`, `tools.exec.host`) and existing guard tests may still pass if nobody adds a new behavioral case. The allowlist drift stays invisible until review catches it manually.

---

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a **focused contract test** that complements (not replaces) `gateway-tool-guard-coverage.test.ts`:

1. **Snapshot lock** — exact sorted contents of `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS` (18 patterns today)
2. **Compact forbidden-path table** — representative high-impact paths that must stay blocked
3. **`replacePaths` guard boundary** — wholesale `agents.list` replacement must still respect the allowlist

Minimal prod change: export the allowlist for tests only (`ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS_FOR_TEST`). No runtime behavior change.

---

## Security / Trust Boundary Context

`assertGatewayConfigMutationAllowed` (`gateway-tool.ts:379`) is the model → operator trust gate. It runs **before** the gateway RPC and applies two independent checks:

```
config.patch / config.apply raw
        │
        ▼
 applyMergePatch (mergeObjectArraysById + optional replacePaths)
        │
        ▼
 collectChangedConfigPaths(current, next)
        │
        ├─► Gate 1: every changed path must match ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS
        │         (prefix match; `*` = one segment wildcard)
        │
        └─► Gate 2: newly enabled dangerous flags blocked
                  (same enumeration as `openclaw security audit`)
```

**Gate 1** is what this PR locks. **Gate 2** (dangerous flags) remains covered by existing guard-coverage cases (e.g. `browser.ssrfPolicy`, `sandbox.docker.dangerouslyAllowContainerNamespaceJoin`).

Public docs already describe the intended contract:

> Agent-driven `gateway config.apply` and `gateway config.patch` edits are fail-closed by default: only a narrow set of low-risk runtime tuning, mention-gating, and visible-reply paths are agent-tunable. Global model defaults and prompt overlays stay operator-controlled.

— [Control plane tools risk](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security#control-plane-tools-risk)

---

## Locked Allowlist (18 patterns)

| Category | Patterns | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Agent runtime tuning (defaults) | `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, `.subagents.thinking`, `.reasoningDefault`, `.fastModeDefault` | Low-risk model behavior knobs |
| Agent runtime tuning (per-agent) | `agents.list[].id`, `.model`, `.thinkingDefault`, `.subagents.thinking`, `.reasoningDefault`, `.fastModeDefault` | Scoped per-agent tuning only |
| Mention gating (depth 1–5) | `channels.*.requireMention` … `channels.*.*.*.*.*.requireMention` | Must cover deepest adapter path (Telegram topic overrides) |
| Visible reply UX | `messages.visibleReplies`, `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies`, `messages.groupChat.unmentionedInbound` | Bounded delivery UX, not secrets/privilege |

**Explicitly NOT on the allowlist** (operator-only): `gateway.auth.*`, `plugins.allow`, `plugins.load.paths`, `tools.exec.*`, `hooks.*`, global `agents.defaults.model`, prompt overlays, sandbox overrides, MCP servers, etc. — already blocked in guard-coverage; this PR adds contract-level regression for three canonical forbidden paths.

---

## New Test Coverage

**File:** `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts`

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `locks the exact allowed path patterns` | Sorted snapshot of all 18 patterns; any add/remove/reorder fails CI |
| `blocks protected path mutations: gateway.auth.token` | Auth secret rewrite blocked |
| `blocks protected path mutations: plugins.allow` | Plugin trust boundary blocked |
| `blocks protected path mutations: tools.exec.host` | Exec routing escalation blocked |
| `allows agents.list wholesale replace via replacePaths when edits stay allowlisted` | `replacePaths: ["agents.list"]` + model-only change passes |
| `blocks agents.list wholesale replace via replacePaths when protected fields change` | `replacePaths: ["agents.list"]` + `sandbox` change still blocked |

### `replacePaths` semantics covered here

- **Without** `replacePaths`: id-keyed merge (default) — already heavily tested in guard-coverage
- **With** `replacePaths: ["agents.list"]`: whole-array replacement is simulated at the **gateway-tool guard** layer
- **Server-side** destructive-array rules (`server.config-patch.test.ts`) are orthogonal; this PR ensures the tool guard still fail-closes protected nested fields even when the caller opts into array replacement

---

## User Impact

- **Runtime:** none
- **Operators:** none
- **Maintainers:** intentional allowlist changes require updating both:
  1. `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS` in `gateway-tool.ts`
  2. `LOCKED_ALLOWLIST` in `gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts`

  That is intentional — widening the agent-tunable surface should be a deliberate, reviewed act.

---

## Evidence

### Local proof

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  6 passed (6)
```

### Diff size

```
src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts                        | +3   (test-only export)
src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts | +103 (contract tests)
```

### Evidence map

| Surface | Entry point | Owner | Caller | Sibling | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway config mutation guard | `assertGatewayConfigMutationAllowed` | `gateway-tool.ts` | `createGatewayTool` config.apply/patch actions | Gateway server `config.patch` RPC | **This PR** + `gateway-tool-guard-coverage.test.ts` |
| Dangerous flag gate | `collectEnabledInsecureOrDangerousFlags` | `dangerous-config-flags.ts` | same guard | `openclaw security audit` | guard-coverage (unchanged) |
| Array merge policy | `applyMergePatch` + `replacePaths` | `merge-patch.ts` | gateway-tool + gateway RPC | `server.config-patch.test.ts` | **This PR** (tool guard slice) + server tests |

---

## Out of Scope / Follow-ups

This PR does **not**:

- Extract `ALLOWED_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATHS` into schema-derived metadata (separate maintenance PR)
- Add security-audit reachability findings for open channels + `gateway` tool exposure (separate audit PR)
- Duplicate all 43 guard-coverage behavioral cases in the contract file

Suggested follow-up if allowlist keeps growing: generate `LOCKED_ALLOWLIST` from a single exported constant or schema artifact to avoid dual-edit friction.

---

## Checklist

- [x] No runtime behavior change
- [x] Test-only export marked `@internal`
- [x] Fail-closed contract: widening allowlist requires explicit test update
- [x] `replacePaths` boundary covered at gateway-tool guard layer
- [ ] CI (pending upstream run after PR open)

---

## Create PR

```sh
gh pr create \
  --title "test(gateway): lock config mutation allowlist contract" \
  --body-file pr-gateway-allowlist-contract-body.md
```

Or open: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/main...hugenshen:codex/gateway-config-allowlist-contract?expand=1
